pc_gate_ledger_notes.language: PIN + DECISION FAMILY, rewritten cycle 6 for coordinator item T-f (M-5). The pinned part is the VALUE: `users.language` is a placeholder SymbolicString on the principal rep (a set-membership test against ~50 AVAILABLE_LANGUAGE_CODES cannot be recorded as equalities without exploding the universe). Its branch-relevant PROPERTIES are recorded decisions, exactly as the `text` pin's are: (1) `<principal>_language_available` (run_dse.rb, minted before the action body) models `ApplicationController#set_locale`'s `I18n.locale = current_user.language` -> `enforce_available_locales!`. Its FALSE arm raises the real `I18n::InvalidLocale` and the run terminates with EXACTLY ONE statement, the Devise users lookup — the multiset M-5 found missing on comments_index. `language = NULL` is the TRUE arm (nil leaves I18n at its default and renders 200), not a third state. (2) The inflected-locale branch (`set_grammatical_gender` -> `current_user.gender` -> the principal's person->profile read) is NOT separately modelled: that exact statement is already in the corpus on both polarities of `SYM_RESULT_ActiveRecord__FinderMethods_devise_user_first_1_person_profile_not_found`, and adversary round 2's R09 drove the endpoint with `language = "pl"` in json/html/mobile with every judge CLEAN (ADVERSARY_REPORT_2.md §1 row N7) — so it costs no evidence.

pc_gate_ledger_notes.id: GATE, added cycle 6 (Rule G census completeness). The app compares the primary key directly: `conversation.ordered_participants - [current_user.person]` (_conversation.haml:11) and `(messages.map(&:author).reverse + participants).uniq` (conversation.rb:61) resolve Array#-/#uniq through AR's `id == id`; `person_link_class`'s `current_user.person == person` (people_helper.rb:84) is the same compare. PC-visible: `(..._row_id == ..._row_id)` PCs are recorded on both sides (targets.rb's class-constant `hash` forces every candidate pair through `eql?`/`==`). The one id compare with NO PC is `_message.html.haml:1`'s `@first_unread_message_id == message.id`: in the sampled model that is x == x (ConcolicIntValue short-circuits a self-compare, cycle-3 R7) and its OTHER outcome is reached through the RECORDED upstream decisions (`unread > 0`, `((- unread) == 0)`, `<list>_index_in_range`) that decide whether `first_unread_message` returns the row or nil. It selects an HTML id attribute only — no data access either way.
